main_dirt.bias_notes: Anti-clockwise (left-handed). A unique oiled sand/dirt oval in Australian TAB racing. Features a 340m home straight. The surface generates intense, heavy sand kickback, creating a massive natural bias toward early front-runners ('E') and pocket pressers ('P') who can race on the lead or fence away from spray. Deep closers ('C') suffer severe kickback penalties.
main_dirt.post_bias: CRITICAL INSIDE RAIL BIAS: In 1000m, 1100m, and 1200m sprint events (including the Palmerston Sprint), inside barriers (stalls 1–4) hold a paramount advantage to secure the rail into the first turn and avoid severe dirt kickback. Outer draws (8+) face heavy ground loss and sand spray.

handicapping_angles.oiled_dirt_kickback_and_speed_bias: Fannie Bay plays like a classic US dirt track. Heavily upgrade early speed ('E') types capable of crossing and securing the fence. Severely downgrade backmarkers ('C') who dislike heavy dirt kickback in their faces.
handicapping_angles.darwin_cup_carnival_shipper_advantage: During the July/August Darwin Cup Carnival (featuring the 2050m Darwin Cup and 1200m Palmerston Sprint), major interstate yards (SA, VIC, WA) send targeted runners. Interstate shippers with proven synthetic or dirt speed figures hold a major class edge over local NT form lines.
handicapping_angles.dirt_experience_filter: Always check for prior dirt, sand, or synthetic surface experience. Horses making their dirt debut from pure lush grass circuits often struggle with the kickback and firm sand footing. Apply a -3.0 point discount to first-time dirt debutants.
handicapping_angles.nt_handicap_weight_penalty: In NT Benchmark handicaps under heavy tropical heat, top weights carrying 60kg+ face an exaggerated physical tax. Favor fit, light-weighted runners receiving apprentice claim relief.
